name: n8n
summary: A self-hostable workflow automation platform that represents business and AI automation as connected nodes, executes workflow runs, and extends the node graph with code, integrations, and human or agent tool steps.

features.name: Node-graph workflow composition
features.description: The fixed repository describes n8n as a visual canvas for AI agents and workflows, and its source is organized as a workspace with workflow and node packages. The README also identifies custom code and extensible nodes as part of the platform boundary.
benefits: Makes multi-step automation visible as connected, reusable node operations
Allows integrations and custom code to participate in one workflow representation
costs: Graph structure, node contracts, and expression evaluation couple otherwise separate integrations
A visual composition does not by itself establish runtime success or transactional behavior

features.name: Persisted execution record and control boundary
features.description: The official CLI documentation exposes executions as addressable records that can be listed, inspected with optional full node data, retried, stopped, and deleted. This is evidence for an explicit execution lifecycle and management boundary, without asserting a particular database or queue implementation.
benefits: Makes run inspection and operator controls explicit
Supports retry and stop operations as separate lifecycle actions
costs: Execution data can be large and sensitive when full node data is included
Retry and stop semantics must account for partial side effects and already-running nodes

features.name: Integration and code extension surface
features.description: The fixed README identifies 1500+ integrations, JavaScript and Python code, npm packages, and extensible custom nodes. These are platform extension points around the workflow representation rather than evidence that every integration shares one implementation.
benefits: Connects external services and custom computation without replacing the workflow model
Allows provider and model choices to vary inside a workflow
costs: Third-party credentials and API behavior expand the failure and security surface
Extension compatibility and package execution require explicit operational controls

features.name: Agent tool and human-approval steps
features.description: The fixed README explicitly describes multi-step AI workflows with logic, tool use, human approvals, and observability. The claim is limited to the documented workflow capability; it does not infer a general agent protocol or guarantee approval enforcement for every node.
benefits: Makes model calls, tools, and approval points composable with ordinary automation
Supports gradual movement from prototype workflows toward operated workflows
costs: Agent output and external tool effects are nondeterministic inputs to later nodes
Approval, retry, and observability policy must be configured at workflow boundaries

mathematical_views.model: Workflow graph execution with externally effectful nodes
mathematical_views.question: How does a connected node graph transform input data through triggers, node operations, agent/tool calls, and terminal outcomes?
assumptions: Nodes and connections form a directed workflow graph
Each node maps input items to output items or an error/stop observation
External calls and model/tool results are environment inputs, not deterministic graph transitions
The view abstracts scheduling, persistence, and exact node concurrency

mathematical_views.question: Which transitions connect an admitted workflow run to running, successful, failed, stopped, retried, or deleted execution observations?
assumptions: Execution records expose the lifecycle operations documented by the CLI
Retry may repeat side effects and is not an exactly-once guarantee
The model does not infer queue topology or persistence isolation from CLI operations alone

mathematical_views.question: How do provider nodes, code nodes, and custom nodes extend a common workflow boundary?
assumptions: An integration or code node is treated as an adapter with a node contract
The README feature list is descriptive product evidence, not proof of identical implementation across integrations
The model abstracts credentials, rate limits, and provider-specific semantics

benefits: Visible composition of heterogeneous automation steps
costs: Graph and node contracts add integration coupling
Retries and full execution data increase operational risk
Extension and credential surface expands maintenance and security work

benefits: AI and approval operations fit ordinary workflows
costs: Nondeterministic model/tool behavior complicates replay and assurance
